Integrating a project into MTDI 5.0

This is the whole procedure, written so a person or an AI agent can follow it without anything else. Integrating a project means writing one manifest and, if needed, one small piece of firmware or software that prints protocol lines. You never edit the pillars to add a project. If a project needs something the pillars cannot express, that is an MTDI improvement (see the end).

1. Create the project

python -m mtdi new astrotech --name "AstroTech"        # inside MTDI Studio
python -m mtdi adopt ../astrotech                       # or: build another repository on MTDI
python -m mtdi create                                   # or: the wizard (+ GitHub, Vercel, Notion, MATLAB)

2. Inventory the measurements

For every quantity the project measures (a sensor reading, a software metric, a network measurement, a security counter), write down:

QuestionBecomes
Which board or program produces it, and how does it reach the computer?a source (serial, tcp, http, python, process, system, replay)
What does one sample look like?the keys the firmware prints
Is it one number or several axes of one quantity?kind: scalar or vector
How do raw numbers become physical units?scale, offset (per key if needed)
What raw values mean "saturated"?raw_range (clipping detection)
What is the smallest real change the sensor resolves?noise_floor (start from the datasheet, then correct it from the measured LOD)
How often should a sample arrive?expected_rate
What field is it?domain, any lowercase word (magnetic, ultrasonic, thermal, compute, network, security, software, …)

Do not invent numbers. If a value is unknown, leave the default and say so in the project README; the Validation Chamber will measure the truth.

3. Make the firmware speak the protocol

One line per sample (firmware/PROTOCOL.md):

KEY=value,KEY=value,_SEQ=42
  • Existing firmware that already prints KEY=value lines needs no change: map its keys.
  • New firmware: start from firmware/mtdi_template_arduino or firmware/mtdi_template_micropython.
  • Software: write a probe that prints protocol lines and run it with the process adapter (projects/network-watch/probe.py), post to /mtdi/ingest (examples/send_http.py), or write a generator for the python adapter.
  • The computer itself: the system adapter needs no code (projects/host-health).
  • Test any line: python -m mtdi parse "DIST_CM=41.7,_SEQ=3".

Never print a placeholder value when the sensor fails. Print nothing: the Validation Chamber turns the silence into a visible fault, while a fake value would be trusted.

4. Write project.json

Field reference: docs/MANIFEST.md. Worked examples: projects/inductra-vaion (vector channels, AC RMS, several sources, domain rules) and projects/ultrasonic-room (scalar, non-electromagnetic).

Add a simulate block to each channel with realistic means and noise, so the project can be checked before the hardware is connected.

5. Add domain knowledge to NVTRA

The universal rules (offline, settling, ambient, one channel dominant, mixed) apply to every project. Add the project's own knowledge as rules on channel signal-to-noise:

{"id": "magnetic_dominance", "when": {"magnetic": ">=6", "electric": "<3"},
 "condition": "Magnetic activity dominant", "text": "…what it physically suggests, and what else could explain it…"}

The first matching rule wins, in order. Text must say what is suggested and what else could cause it. NVTRA never claims more than the evidence.

6. Write Aether

aether.purpose, story, authorship, quote: why the project exists and who made it. It is shown, never scored.

7. Verify

python -m mtdi check projects/astrotech                   # manifest is valid, channel map is right
python -m mtdi run projects/astrotech --simulate          # every page renders, pillars respond
python -m mtdi run projects/astrotech --record s.jsonl    # real hardware; keep the evidence
python -m unittest discover tests                         # nothing else broke

On real hardware, open the Validation Chamber: every channel connected, rate near expected_rate, no clipping at rest. Then set noise_floor from the measured LOD/3. Then in Environmental Intelligence: let it learn, lock it, save the environment.

8. Record it

  • Add a row to the Projects table in README.md.
  • Add an entry to CHANGELOG.md.
  • Write projects/<id>/README.md: what was mapped, what is assumed, what is not carried over.

Improving MTDI itself

If a project needs something no manifest field expresses (a new transform, a new adapter, a new factor), change the pillar generically so every project benefits. Keep all projects passing, add a test, and note it in CHANGELOG.md as an MTDI change. MTDI's version moves (5.0 → 5.1) when a pillar's behaviour changes, not when a project is added.
